sentences.text:
Order 
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.660/2023 dated 07.08.2023 registered at Police Station Maihar, District Satna (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 376, 376(2) (n) and 506 of IPC.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 08.08.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicant is a permanent resident of district and is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.
This second bail application has been argued on the basis of testimony of prosecution witnesses recorded before the trial Court.
The earlier bail application was dismissed under M.Cr.C.No.43950/2023 vide order dated 2 MCRC-15546-2024 14.12.2023.

The reason for dismissal of said application was that the applicant was the employer of prosecutrix who was abusing her sexually since 21.05.2023, on the basis of obscene videos which he was using for blackmailing her.
It was observed while dismissing the earlier bail application that obscene data was recovered from the mobile phone of the applicant through FSL.

sentences.text: 1 was a consenting party as she did not immediately report the matter but the Court did not consider it as a legitimate ground to allow the bail application.

6. In this second bail application again the ground that prosecutrix was a consenting party has been raised on the ground of delay in lodging the FIR and also in the light of statements of Medical Officer.
It has also been argued that the fake I.D. was created by victim on herself on Instagram.

7. Having considered these grounds and also the statements recorded on oath before the trial Court,
it cannot be inferred at this stage that prosecutrix was a consenting party and merely creating a fake I.D. on Instagram does not apparently have any bearing on the merits of the case.

Further, the statements of S.I. Mohini Sharma (PW-8) reveal that Exhibit-A recovered from applicant contained obscene videos about sexual act committed with victim and it also contained obscene photographs.
It has been claimed by prosecutrix that she was being subjected to repeated sexual assault by the applicant under threats of sending these videos and photos to the acquaintances of prosecutrix.
In contrast, there was no argument submitted on this bail application as to why these obscene videos and photographs were available in the mobile phone of applicant.

8. Having considered these facts and finding no substantial change in circumstances, this Court does not find it fit to release the applicant on bail.
9.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.
